title: Social Media Strategy for Small Teams: Do Less, Better
content:
Small teams often try to run social media the way large marketing departments do — five platforms, daily posting, a content calendar planned months out. That approach usually collapses within a few weeks, not because the strategy is wrong, but because it was never sized for the team running it.

Pick one platform first

Spreading thin across five platforms means being mediocre on all of them. Pick the one where your actual customers spend time, get good at it, and only expand once that channel runs on its own momentum.

Build a repeatable structure, not a rigid calendar

Instead of planning exact posts months ahead, build a rotation of content types — a tip, a behind-the-scenes look, a customer story, a product highlight — and cycle through them. This removes the pressure of coming up with something entirely new every time while still keeping content varied.

Automate the mechanical parts, not the thinking

Scheduling, cross-posting, and formatting are mechanical tasks that eat time without adding value. The strategic parts — what to say, who it's for — still need a human. Automating the former frees up real time for the latter.

A small team with a focused, sustainable system will consistently outperform a small team trying to imitate a large one.
